{{Short description|none}}
{{pp-semi-indef}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=August 2020}}
Many changes in the [[Grand Slam (Tennis)|Grand Slam tennis tournaments]] have affected the number of titles won by various players during its history. These changes have included the opening of the French national championships to international players in 1925, the elimination of the challenge round in 1922, and the admission of professional players in 1968 (the start of the [[History of tennis#Open Era|Open Era]]).<ref>{{cite web |title=Grand Slam Timeline |url=https://www.ultimatetennisstatistics.com/tournamentLevelTimeline?level=G |website=ultimatetennisstatistics.com |access-date=8 September 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Grand Slam title winners |url=https://www.grandslamhistory.com/stats/grand-slam/all/mens-singles |website=grandslamhistory.com |access-date=8 September 2021}}</ref>

All of these tournaments have been listed based on the modern definition of a tennis major, rather than when they were officially recognized by the [[ILTF]]. The Grand Slam tournaments are the annual four major tennis events played in the Open Era, which began in 1968, superseding the Amateur Era. The [[Australian Open#History|Australian]] and [[US Open (tennis)#History|U.S.]] tournaments were officially recognized by the ILTF in 1924, and the [[French Open#History|French Championships]] followed a year later in 1925 when it became open to all international players. The [[United States Lawn Tennis Association]] (USLTA) had several grievances with the ILTF and refused to join when it was formed in 1913.<ref>{{cite book | title=The Encyclopedia of Tennis | publisher=Viking Press | publication-date=1974 | last=Robertson | first=Max | pages=28–30}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Hadlich|first=Gui|title=What Are Tennis Grand Slams? (Easy Guide)|url=https://mytennishq.com/what-are-tennis-grand-slams-easy-guide/|access-date=17 September 2021|website=My Tennis HQ|date=14 May 2021 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Tennis {{!}} Grand Slams {{!}} Australian Open {{!}} French Open {{!}} Majors {{!}} US Open {{!}} Wimbledon|url=https://www.tennisct.com/tennis-grand-slams|access-date=17 September 2021|website=Tennis {{!}} Play Tennis {{!}} CT {{!}} Connecticut {{!}} Stamford CT {{!}} Covid Tennis {{!}} Safest Sport {{!}} Tennis Blog {{!}} Tennis Lessons|archive-date=31 January 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220131003401/https://www.tennisct.com/tennis-grand-slams|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=29 September 2020|title=Tennis Grand Slams – The Big 4|url=https://improves.co/tennis-grand-slams/|access-date=17 September 2021|website=Improves}}</ref>

From 1913 to 1923, there were three official championships recognized by the ILTF:
* [[World Grass Court Championships]] – Wimbledon.
* [[World Hard Court Championships]], held in Paris on clay courts.
* [[World Covered Court Championships]], held in Europe on an indoor wood surface.
During that same time period the USLTA recognized the U.S. National Championships
* [[US Open (tennis)|U.S. National Championships]], held in New York on grass.

{{Multiple images|perrow=2|total_width=250|
|image1=Djokovic EBN17 (26) (35046150944).jpg
|caption1=[[Novak Djokovic]] holds the all-time record of 24 major singles titles, including a record 10 [[Australian Open]] titles. He is the only singles player to hold all four majors simultaneously on [[#Non-calendar year Grand Slam|three different surfaces]] (2016), and the only one to complete a triple [[#Career Grand Slam|Career Grand Slam]] (2023).
|image2=Rafael Nadal 2011 Roland Garros 2011-crop.jpg
|caption2=[[Rafael Nadal]] holds an all-time record of 14 [[French Open]] titles, the most at any slam in tennis history. He is the second man in the [[History of tennis#Open Era|Open Era]] to complete a double Career Grand Slam (2022).
|image3=Roger Federer (26 June 2009, Wimbledon) 3 cropped.jpg
|caption3=[[Roger Federer]] holds an all-time record of 8 [[The Championships, Wimbledon|Wimbledon]] titles. He also held the most major titles in singles between 2009 and 2022.
|image4=Bill-Tilden.jpg
|caption4=[[Bill Tilden]] won 10 major singles titles in the 1920s, including an all-time record of seven [[US Open (tennis)|U.S. Championships]] titles.
|image5=Don Budge 1938.jpg
|caption5=[[Don Budge]] is the only man to have won six consecutive major singles titles, from [[1937 Wimbledon Championships – Men's singles|Wimbledon 1937]] to [[1938 U.S. National Championships – Men's singles|U.S. Championships 1938]], and the first player ever to complete a [[#Grand Slam|Grand Slam]] (1938).
|image6=Ken Rosewall (1970) (cropped).jpg
|caption6=[[Ken Rosewall]] holds a record 15 [[Major professional tennis tournaments before the Open Era#Professional majors|Pro Major]] titles, and [[Tennis male players statistics#Most major singles titles|23 major titles overall]], counting both amateur and professional circuits.
|image7=Roy Emerson 1969 (cropped).jpg
|caption7=[[Roy Emerson]] was the first man in history to win each major title twice (1967), and the only man to have completed a Career Grand Slam in both [[#Career Grand Slam|singles]] and [[List of Grand Slam men's doubles champions#Individual 2|doubles]].
|image8=Rodney George Laver.jpg
|caption8=[[Rod Laver]] is the only man to complete a Grand Slam more than once in his career, in 1962 as an amateur and in 1969 as a professional.
|image9=Pete Sampras.jpg
|caption9=[[Pete Sampras]] won 14 major singles titles in his career, including seven titles at Wimbledon.
|image10=Andre Agassi Indian Wells 2006.jpg
|caption10=[[Andre Agassi]] was the first man to complete a Career Grand Slam across three different surfaces (1999), and the first to win a [[#Career Golden Slam|Career Golden Slam]] (winning the four majors and an [[List of Olympic medalists in tennis#Men's singles|Olympic singles gold medal]]).
}}

{{notelist|1|refs=
{{efn|name=FR|French Championship from 1891 to 1924 was open only to specific club members.{{efn|name=WHCC}} Titles are not counted toward major totals.}}
{{efn|name=WM|Wimbledon from 1878 to 1921 was decided in a [[Glossary of tennis terms#Challenge Round|Challenge Round]] match.}}
{{efn|name=US|US Championship from 1884 to 1911 was decided in a Challenge Round match.}}
{{efn|name=FO|The French Championships opened itself to international competitors and renamed as Championnats Internationaux de France (de tennis). See [[World Hard Court Championships|WHCC]].}}
{{efn|name=WHCC|The [[World Hard Court Championships]] which was held in Paris on clay courts, has often been considered the true precursor to the French Open.}}
{{efn|name=AO19|1919 Australasian Championships was held in January 1920, before the 1920 Australasian Championships.}}
{{efn|name=AO23|1923 Australasian Championships was held in August, after Wimbledon and before the US National Championships.}}
{{efn|name=AO27|Australasian Championships was renamed to Australian Championships.}}
{{efn|name=FOWWII|French Championships held between 1941 and 1945 are not recognized by the tournament organizer. See [[Tournoi de France (tennis)|Tournoi de France]].}}
{{efn|name=FO46|French Open was held in July, after Wimbledon from 1946 to 1947 due to the effects in the [[aftermath of World War II]].}}
{{efn|name=AO77| Australian Open was held in December, after the US Open from 1977 to 1985.}}
{{efn|name=Kriekusa| Johan Kriek became a naturalised US citizen after originally representing South Africa.}}
{{efn|name=FO20|2020 French Open was held in September, after the US Open, due to the COVID-19 pandemic.}}
}}

== Grand Slam achievements ==
{{Main|Grand Slam (tennis)}}

These are players who achieved some form of a tennis [[Grand Slam (tennis)|Grand Slam]]. They include a Grand Slam, non-calendar year Grand Slam, Career Grand Slam, Career Golden Slam, and Career Super Slam. No male player has won a single season [[List of Grand Slam women's singles champions#Golden Slam|Golden Slam]]. The tennis [[History of tennis#Open Era|Open Era]] began in 1968, after the [[1968 Australian Open|Australian Open]] and before the [[1968 French Open|French Open]].
